# Code of Conduct

This Code of Conduct applies to all repositories of the **KIT-IWU-HydroEng** organization, unless a repository provides its own `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`.

## Our pledge

We, as members, contributors and maintainers, want participation in our projects to be a harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of age, body size, visible or invisible disability, ethnicity, sex characteristics, gender identity and expression, level of experience, education, socio-economic status, nationality, personal appearance, race, religion, or sexual identity and orientation.

We pledge to act and interact in ways that contribute to an open, welcoming, diverse, inclusive and healthy community, in which researchers, students and users from any background can share their work and learn from each other.

## Our standards

Examples of behaviour that contributes to a positive environment:

- being respectful and considerate towards others, including people with different viewpoints, experiences and levels of expertise
- giving and gracefully accepting constructive feedback on code, methods and results
- discussing scientific disagreements openly and objectively, focusing on arguments and evidence rather than on people
- giving credit where it is due, acknowledging the work and ideas of others
- taking responsibility for our mistakes, apologizing to those affected, and learning from the experience
- helping newcomers, such as students, become familiar with our projects

Examples of unacceptable behaviour:

- the use of sexualized language or imagery, and sexual attention or advances of any kind
- trolling, insulting or derogatory comments, and personal or political attacks
- public or private harassment
- publishing others' private information, such as a physical or email address, without their explicit permission
- presenting others' code, data or ideas as one's own, or removing attribution
- other conduct that could reasonably be considered inappropriate in a professional or academic setting

## Scope

This Code of Conduct applies within all spaces of our repositories, such as issues, pull requests, discussions, code reviews and commit messages. It also applies when someone officially represents the group in public spaces, for example when using an official email address or acting as an appointed representative at an online or offline event.

## Responsibilities

Maintainers are responsible for clarifying and enforcing our standards of acceptable behaviour and will take appropriate and fair corrective action in response to any behaviour they deem inappropriate, threatening, offensive or harmful.

Maintainers have the right to remove, edit or reject comments, commits, code, wiki edits, issues and other contributions that do not follow this Code of Conduct, and will communicate the reasons for moderation decisions when appropriate.

## Reporting

Instances of abusive, harassing or otherwise unacceptable behaviour may be reported to the maintainers. If the report concerns one of the maintainers, you may instead contact another member of the group directly.

All reports will be reviewed and investigated promptly and fairly. Everyone involved in handling a report is obliged to respect the privacy and security of the person who reported the incident.

## Enforcement guidelines

Maintainers will follow these guidelines when deciding on the consequences of an action they consider a violation of this Code of Conduct:

1. **Correction**: for inappropriate language or other behaviour considered unprofessional or unwelcome. The person receives a private, written warning explaining the nature of the violation and why the behaviour was inappropriate. A public apology may be requested.
2. **Warning**: for a single violation or a series of actions. The person receives a warning with consequences for continued behaviour, and for a specified period of time must not interact with the people involved, including through unsolicited interaction with those enforcing the Code of Conduct. Violating these terms may lead to a temporary or permanent ban.
3. **Temporary ban**: for a serious violation, including sustained inappropriate behaviour. The person is temporarily banned from any interaction or public communication with the community for a specified period of time. Violating these terms may lead to a permanent ban.
4. **Permanent ban**: for demonstrating a pattern of violations, including sustained inappropriate behaviour, harassment of an individual, or aggression towards or disparagement of groups of people. The person is permanently banned from any public interaction within the community.

Members of KIT remain subject to the rules and regulations of KIT in addition to this Code of Conduct.

## Attribution

This Code of Conduct is adapted from the [Contributor Covenant](https://www.contributor-covenant.org), version 2.1, available at <https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct.html>. The enforcement guidelines are inspired by [Mozilla's code of conduct enforcement ladder](https://github.com/mozilla/diversity).
